{{nihongo|'''Isono Shrine'''|伊曽乃神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iyo Province]].

[[File:Isono 14.jpg|thumb|220px|'''Danjiri'' across the Kamo River]]'''Isono Shrine'' (Isono Jinja, {{old font|'''Isono Shrine''}}) is located in Nakano, {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|Q123376|qid=Q123376}}{{ill|Saijō, Ehime|ar|ساجيو (إهيمه)|azb|سایجو، اهیمه|ce|Сайдзё|ceb|Saijō-shi|de|Saijō|eo|Sajĝo|es|Saijō (Ehime)|fa|سایجو، اهیمه|fi|Saijō|fr|Saijō|gl|Saijō|hu|Szaidzsó|id|Saijō, Ehime|it|Saijō|ja|西条市|kab|Saijo|ko|사이조시|mg|Saijō|mzn|سایجو، اهیمه|nl|Saijo|no|Saijō|pl|Saijō|pt|Saijo|ro|Saijō|ru|Сайдзё|sh|Saijō, Ehime|sr|Саиџо|sv|Saijo|tg|Саиҷо|tl|Saijō|tr|Saijō|tt|Сайдзё|uk|Сайджьо (Ехіме)|ur|سائیجو، اہیمے|uz|Saydzyo|vi|Saijō, Ehime|war|Saijō, Ehime|zh|西條市|zh_classical|西條市|zh_min_nan|Saizyô-chhī|zh_yue|西條|qid=Q633945}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}). {{ill|Q712534|lt=old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Kokuhei Chūsha|qid=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha}}, and currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinmon}} is the "gosho car".

It is known as the shrine where the largest danjiri is dedicated during the gorgeous "{{ill|Saijo Festival|Q11628729|qid=Q11628729}}". In ancient times, it was also called ``Isono Shrine''.

=== Enshrined God ===
The following two deities are enshrined. It has two pillars and is collectively called "Isonojin" <ref>[http://www.isonojinja.or.jp/%E7%94%B1%E7%B7%92/ History] (official website). </ref>.
:* {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602}}'s {{ill|Mitama|Q495568|qid=Q495568|lt=Aratama}}
:* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Bukoku Kobetsu no Mikoto}}

Initially, there was only one deity enshrined, and it was called ``Isonokami''. According to the shrine's biography and old records, the first troupe was Amaterasu Omikami's Aratama, and later Bukoku Kobetsu no Mikoto was added to form two troupes. The main deity, Amaterasu Omikami, is enshrined in the center of the inner sanctum of the main shrine, and the side shrine deity, Bukoku Kobetsu no Mikoto, is enshrined to the left.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
According to the shrine's legend, in the 7th year of the 13th Emperor Seimu, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takekuni Kobetsu no Mikoto}} (the prince of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}), the founder of Iyo Mimurabetsu, It is said that the development of the {{ill|Tōyo region|Q9067702|qid=Q9067702}} began with the worship of {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602}}, the {{ill|Ancestors of the Emperor|Q11581090|qid=Q11581090}}. It is said that Takekuni Kobetsu-no-Mikoto worshiped the spirit of Amaterasu Omikami and traveled to Iyo from {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}, arriving at Mifunemori in present-day Sakuhi City, the same city (``Mifunemori'' is located along the Mifune River).

During {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|Q317980|qid=Q317980}}'s {{ill|Taika (era)|Q1077930|qid=Q1077930}} ({{ill|645|Q31040|qid=Q31040}}-{{ill|650|Q30179|qid=Q30179}}) There is a theory that the name ``Kamino District'' (later {{ill|Nii district|ja|新居郡|zh|新居郡|qid=Q11082347}}) came from the fact that gods were already enshrined at Isono Shrine and other places, and this area was called Kaminochi (land of the gods).

=== Outline ===
[[File:Isonojinzya20220226 4a.jpg|thumb|First torii and throwing stones and {{ill|Mount Ishizuchi|Q2744214|qid=Q2744214}}]]
In the ancient literature, in the 2nd year ({{ill|766|Q30564|qid=Q30564}} of "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}" {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|Q1373181|qid=Q1373181}} 2nd year ({{ill|766|Q30564|qid=Q30564}}), "Isonokami" was given the rank of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}, which is lower than the junior fourth rank, and {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711|lt=Kobe}}It is written that 5 smokes will be used. “{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}” {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=In the 1st year of Daido}} ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}), 15 units from Iyo Province were allocated to "Isonokami" as Kanbe at that time; Ten of them are based on the sign of October of the first year of Tenpyo Jingo ({{ill|765|Q31216|qid=Q31216}}), and five are based on the sign of December 3 of the second year of Tenpyo Jingo ({{ill|766|Q30564|qid=Q30564}}).

In the subsequent {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi}}, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} It is written that he was promoted to the lower rank of Sho4 in the 8th year ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), to the higher rank of the upper fourth rank in the 12th year of Jogan ({{ill|870|Q23629|qid=Q23629}}), and to the junior third rank in the 17th year of Jogan ({{ill|875|Q23816|qid=Q23816}}).{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, there is "Isano Shrine" in Arai District, Iyo Province. It is listed as ``Meishin Taisha'' and is listed as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}.

In the first year of {{ill|Eiji (era)|Q1194167|qid=Q1194167}} ({{ill|1141|Q19613|qid=Q19613}}), he was conferred the rank of {{ill|Senior First Rank|Q11123258|qid=Q11123258}} and was given an imperial plaque by {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|azb|سوتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Сутоку|ca|Sutoku|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوتۆکو|cs|Sutoku|de|Sutoku|es|Sutoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوتوکو|fr|Sutoku|hak|Sutoku Thiên-fòng|he|סוטוקו|id|Kaisar Sutoku|it|Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|ko|스토쿠 천황|mr|सुतोकु|nl|Sutoku|pl|Sutoku|pt|Sutoku|ru|Император Сутоку|sh|Car Sutoku|simple|Sutoku|sv|Sutoku|sw|Sutoku wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิซูโตกุ|tl|Emperador Sutoku|tr|Sutoku|uk|Імператор Сутоку|vi|Thiên hoàng Sutoku|yo|Emperor Sutoku|zh|崇德天皇|zh_min_nan|Sutoku Thian-hông|qid=Q349287}}.

* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 8th year ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}) Leap March 7th, from the upper fourth rank to the lower rank of the fourth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'') - Written as ``Isonokami.''
* August 28, 12th year of Jogan ({{ill|870|Q23629|qid=Q23629}}), from Sho4i Lower to Sho4i Upper (``Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - Written as ``Isonokami.''
* March 29, 17th year of the Jogan era ({{ill|875|Q23816|qid=Q23816}}), from the top of the fourth rank to the third rank of junior rank ("Nihon Sandai Jirroku") - Written as "Isonokami".

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Isinojinzya20220226 1.jpg|thumb|Headquarters]]
* Ichino Torii: Made of stone. The Stone Hammer God's Throwing Stone is on the right.
* Ninotorii: made of copper
* Stone pillar gate
* In front of the Shinto gate: The Danjiri parade is performed in this space.
* Hall of worship: The main hall of worship faces east because the enshrined deity is Amaterasu Omikami, but since the approach from the first torii gate is in the direction of the entrance from the city area, the approach and the main hall are at right angles.
* Main shrine: Built in 1945. Shinmei-zukuri made of all-hinoki cypress.
* Konohana Sakuyahime ({{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|az|Konohanasakuya|ca|Konohana no Sakuya hime|de|Konohanasakuyahime|fa|کونوهاناساکویا-هیمه|fr|Konohana-no-Sakuya|it|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|コノハナノサクヤビメ|ko|고노하나노사쿠야비메|mni|ꯀꯣꯅꯣꯍꯅꯁꯀꯨꯌ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Konohanasakuya-hime|ru|Коноханасакуя-химэ|sv|Konohanasakuyahime|th|เซ็นเง็ง|vi|Konohana Sakuya Hime|zh|木花開耶姬|qid=Q1781862}}) Statue of Life: The second daughter of Oyama Gigami. Unveiled on March 18, 2013.
* Mikoshi storage: Stores one adult mikoshi and one children's mikoshi.
* Shrine: The sacred tree in front of the shrine grounds is 30 meters high and 5.5 meters in circumference, estimated to be 700 years old and is one of Saijo City's 50 famous water trees. Selected in March 1991.
* Treasure Hall: 300 yen for adults, 100 yen for children
* Isano Bunko
* Funeral hall
* A haiku monument: Kobayashi Issa's ``Is there a drop of flowers on my head?'' is along with a sub-inscription on the right just beyond the Ninotorii gate. ``Shinba ni Uchihaki Kuni de Hatsumode'' is on the left. ``Looking up at the glistening camphor tree, breathing in the breath as the mikoshi floats along the river, wearing Shichi-Go-San clothes with refreshing smiles,'' is located on the south side of the parking lot.
* Parking: Large parking lot available and free of charge. Cannot be used during regular festivals.

The genealogy of the Arai clan, a powerful clan in the Iyo region, was copied around 1281 by {{ill|Gyōnen|fr|Gyōnen|ja|凝然|zh|凝然|qid=Q3122771}}, a member of the family and a monk at Todaiji Temple. Together with the Wake genealogy ({{ill|Mii-dera|Q1756307|qid=Q1756307}} collection in Shiga Prefecture) and the {{ill|Ama Clan Genealogy|Q11559330|qid=Q11559330|lt=Kaifu genealogy}} ({{ill|Kono Shrine|Q705126|qid=Q705126}} collection in Kyoto prefecture), it is called one of Japan's three greatest ancient genealogy trees. === Reitaisai ===
; {{ill|Saijo Festival|Q11628729|qid=Q11628729|lt=Isono Shrine Annual Festival}}October 15th and 16th<ref> "Encyclopedia of Annual Events" p48 First edition published on May 23, 1958 {{ill|Nishitsunoi Masayoshi|Q11629502|qid=Q11629502}} Edited by Tokyodo Publishing</ref>.
: {{ill|Dashi|qid=Dashi|lt=Dashi}} (comfort floats/stands) 77, {{ill|Taikodai|Q11444734|qid=Q11444734|lt='''Mikoshi'''}} (Mikoshi floats. It is said that the number of floats dedicated to one shrine is {{ill|List of records of Japan|Q6636181|qid=Q6636181|lt=Most in Japan}}, and is unprecedented in other regions. Early on the 15th, ``Danjiri'' will enter the shrine and perform in front of our shrine gate. On the evening of the 16th, the festival ends when the ``Kami-san'' crosses the river (Kamo River, about 1km north of our company), and 11 ``Danjiri'' from the local Kobe area block the way of the ``Kami-san'' as they try to return home.

=== Tradition ===
[[File:Isono 0ø.jpg|180px|thumb|Throwing Stone of the Stone Hammer God]]
According to local legend, a long time ago, the goddess Isano and the male god {{ill|Mount Ishizuchi|Q2744214|qid=Q2744214}} met on the banks of the Kamo River. The two fell in love, and the goddess forced them to marry. However, the male god refused, saying that he could not marry her because he had to continue his training at Mt. Ishizuchi. Furthermore, women are not allowed to accompany them on Mt. Ishizuchi, so they are not allowed to accompany them. ``Once I finish my training, I will get married, so I want you to wait until then. I will throw three large stones from the top of the mountain, so build a mansion where the middle stone falls and wait,'' he said as he climbed the mountain. Shortly after, three stones flew down from Mt. Ishizuchi, and Isano Shrine was built where the middle stone fell. Today, next to the first torii gate of Isono Shrine, there remains a stone that is said to be the throwing stone of the stone hammer god.
